I grew up watching Star Trek, and yes, I even went to the conventions.

However, as a much older and wiser man, this show is filled with so much communist propaganda it makes your head spin.

In the episode of Star Trek: The Next Generation, The Pegasus, the entire crew basically hands over classified intelligence to the Romulans under the pretense of abiding by the "treaty" that forbids the Federation from possessing cloaking devices even though the Romulans can use theirs without hindrance. Star Fleet even went so far as to remove and prosecute all of the high level officials involved in the development of the phase cloaking device. I'm sure decimating your internal organization is okay in some kind of fantasy reality, but had this been anything other than fantasy, the tentative cease fire between the Romulans and Star Fleet would have probably ended when the Romulans saw an apparent weakness to exploit. Regardless, this was an extremely hypocritical move because of the danger the Federation puts all of its members in by expecting people to adhere to some kind of perceived notion of enlightened morality at the expense of common sense. This is basically saying that it's okay to take a knife to a gun fight because taking a gun would be too mean.

Later in Deep Space Nine, Sisco starts taking the Defiant into the Gamma Quadrant while it is equipped with a cloaking device. At first they give some lip service to the precedent they set earlier by mandating a Romulan liaison's presence on board to be the sole operator of the cloaking device but as you can imagine, it wasn't too much longer after this that they just ditched the liaison altogether and operated the cloak with impunity. It's funny how there was no more mention of the treaty. Sure you could make the argument that the extraordinary measures were required because of the heightened threat posed by the Jem'Hadar, but what about the threat posed by the Romulan Tal Shiar, what about tenuous relations with the Klingons, what about tenuous relations with the Cardassians, to whom the Federation even ceded entire worlds? And it's bullshit the Star Fleet "isn't a military organization." For someone to "not be a military organization," they sure as hell participated in a shit load of military operations.

The writers were just too god damned lazy and hypocritical to come up with an idea to correct this. There is no reason why Star Fleet should have been intentionally imposing a weakness on itself. But there it was. Time after time, the characters in the Star Trek universe sacrifice common sense to pursue "enlightened" decisions that would no doubt end horribly in a reality that is not one of fantasy.

So how is this communist propaganda? The audience is brainwashed into believing that there will be an outcome other than defeat when one pursues avenues of self-imposed weakness. These stories are priming people to make decisions that defy common sense, and because they take place in the realm of fantasy, they always end well for the characters. In real life, imposing these weaknesses on yourself will allow your enemies to make quick work of you. You will be helplessly and mercilessly slaughtered, with no second thought of "morality."

There are many other examples of horrendous hypocrisy in this show when it comes to "morality" and what the Federation did to the Maquis by just handing their entire planets over to the Cardassians for the sake of appeasement, but I can't stand dissecting it much longer.

TL;DR: I used to like Star Trek but now I watch it only as a cautionary tale.
